rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of global replacement regex in hook function leading to unexpected placeholder replacement
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used a global regex /%/g to replace all percent signs in the script command, but the patch changes this to replace only the first occurrence of '%'. This can cause scripts with multiple placeholders to be incorrectly rendered, affecting script execution.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the placeholder replacement back to use a global regex (/%,/g) to replace all occurrences of '%' in config.scripts[action].

rawFindings.title: Test expectations no longer match updated placeholder usage in script commands
rawFindings.explanation: The tests were modified to expect fewer suffixed parts in filenames (e.g., 'preinstall_packageName' instead of 'preinstall_packageName_packageName'), reflecting the change that only one placeholder is replaced instead of multiple. This reduces test coverage of scripts with multiple placeholders and may mask regressions.
rawFindings.suggestion: Update tests to cover both cases or revert changes to the test strings to maintain coverage for multiple placeholder replacements.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect global replacement of placeholder '%' in script command
rawFindings.explanation: The original code replaced all occurrences of '%' in the script command string with ordered package names, which allowed multiple placeholders to be replaced. The change limits replacement to only the first occurrence by passing '%' directly (without global flag) to mout.string.replace. This may cause unexpected behavior if the script contains multiple '%' placeholders intended to be replaced.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using a RegExp with global flag for placeholder replacement: Use var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g'); and then call mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], placeholder, orderedPackages.join(' ')); to replace all '%' occurrences consistently.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect placeholder replacement regex usage in `hook` function
rawFindings.explanation: The `hook` function uses `new RegExp('%', 'g')` as `placeholder` to replace all '%' characters with the joined package names. The change replaces this with a string '%' instead. The mout.string.replace function is expected to replace only the first occurrence when passed a string, not all occurrences.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert line 87 to use `var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g');` to replace all '%' placeholders globally rather than only the first occurrence.
